story_text:
[画像: Co Print Quadro, a waste-free multicolor and multi-material 3D printer with four independent toolheads on a single X-axis and a 300 × 300 × 300 mm build volume, with icons for 1-second color change, purge-free printing and multi-material printing.]
[画像: Quadro key features: about 1 s toolchange, 300 × 300 × 300 mm build volume, Zero Waste Mode, up to 90% less filament waste and 70% less print time, a dual-motor Y-axis with 10,000 mm/s² acceleration, its own motor and belt for every toolhead, PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA and ABS, the sealed QDock Station, fully automatic calibration in QuadrOS and the open-source Co Slicer.]
## Meet Co Print Quadro
[画像: Meet Co Print Quadro]
Meet Quadro, a multicolor, multi-material 3D printer with four independent toolheads on one axis, each loaded with its own filament and ready the whole time. When the color changes, the next head simply starts printing while the last one parks in its sealed station.
The result is up to 90% less filament waste and up to 5X faster⁴ multicolor prints than single-nozzle systems, in a 300 × 300 × 300 mm build volume with four materials in one print. Quadro comes from Co Print, the team that has been building color systems for 3D printers since 2019.
Nothing swaps. Nothing purges. Every color already loaded, waiting its turn.
[画像: Quadro printing in a colorful maker studio as its four toolheads take turns, and kids playing with a multicolor print it made.]
## Why We Built It
[画像: Why we built it: color shouldn't cost this much.]
Every multicolor printer sends you a bill. Single-nozzle systems pay it in plastic: before each color change the old color is pushed out of the nozzle, and on a four-color print that pile can outweigh the model itself. Tool and nozzle changers pay it in mechanics: more parts moving on every change, and more parts that have to stay perfectly aligned.
Quadro pays neither bill.
[画像: Four problems Quadro solves: purge waste bigger than the model becomes up to 90% less waste; hard-to-remove supports become clean soluble PVA supports; toolchange problems become four heads on one axis with no swaps; single-material prototypes become multi-material prototypes.]
## What Makers Are Saying
[画像: From the creators: what makers are saying.]
[画像: Quadro printing a red multicolor dragon figure in a studio lined with filament spools.]
## Nothing Swaps
[画像: Nothing swaps: how it works.]
Existing multi-toolhead 3D printing solutions rely on swapping either entire toolheads or nozzles. Toolchangers must park the previous head, move to the next one, and pick it up before printing can continue. Nozzle-swapping systems must retract and cut the filament, park the old nozzle, pick up a new one, and feed the filament back in.
Quadro changes everything.
No picking up. No putting down. No swapping.
One toolhead simply slides out of the way, and the next takes its place in as little as 1 second. All four toolheads stay mounted, loaded, and ready to print.
[画像: IQEX™ architecture: one toolhead leaves as the next arrives.]
IDEX printers put two independent extruders on one gantry. IQEX™, Independent Quad Extruder, puts four on a single X-axis. Each toolhead has its own stepper motor, belt and pulley, driven from two motors on each side. They take turns or stay out of each other's way, but no head is ever picked up, put down or handed over.
[画像: Quadro's four toolheads moving independently on one X-axis: one slides out of the way as the next takes its place.]
[画像: 1-second toolchange, up to 5X faster printing.]
[画像: About 1 s color change, measured head to head at 1.00 s, with 7 motors moving together and 0 swaps: no unloading, no cutting, no coupling.]
The next toolhead starts heating about 30 seconds before it's needed, while the current one is still printing. When it's time, seven motors move together: the outgoing head returns to its station as the incoming one takes its place. No unloading, no cutting, no coupling to lock. Measured from one head to the next: 1.00 s.³
[画像: 1-second toolchange on Quadro: toolhead 1 to 2 in 1.00 s, to 3 in 1.40 s and to 4 in 1.57 s.]
Quadro delivers significant time and filament savings compared to traditional single-nozzle multi-color printers. But the advantages don't stop there. Thanks to IQEX™ technology, Quadro also offers faster tool changes than the latest toolchanger and nozzle-swapping systems.
To put this to the test, we compared five different 4-color models printed on Quadro, a toolchanger, and a latest-generation large-format bed-slinger. All three printers used the same model sizes, 0.4 mm nozzles, and 0.2 mm layer heights for a consistent comparison.
Quadro completed the prints up to 70% faster while using up to 90% less filament waste, proving that multi-color printing can be faster, more efficient, and far more affordable.¹
Most multicolor printers build one model at a time. IDEX printers can build two at once, but with one head per print, each copy comes out in a single color. With four heads on one axis, Quadro doesn't have to choose: toolheads 1 and 2 build the first print, toolheads 3 and 4 build the second, side by side and at the same time, each in two colors. Every head runs on its own motor and belt, so the two pairs work in step without getting in each other's way.
Load different colors in each pair and the same model comes off the bed in two colorways. Two finished color prints in about the time of one, made for batches, small shops, print farms and anything you need more than one of.
[画像: Print time and filament waste for five four-color models on Quadro, a toolchanger and a single-nozzle printer. Example, a football helmet by @Geek3Designs: Quadro 20 h 36 min and 58.69 g of waste, toolchanger 23 h 40 min and 114.14 g, single nozzle 1 day 21 h 38 min and 301.4 g.]
[画像: QDock Station™: parked, sealed, ready.]
When a toolhead finishes, its filament retracts about 1 mm and the nozzle cools to around 140°C on the way to its station. Once docked, the tip is sealed with a heat-resistant, nozzle-safe material. Not just idle: sealed. Nothing drips on the bed, nothing strings across your model, and no color bleeds into the next one.
[画像: Quadro's QDock Station seals idle nozzles: a test print without sealing shows stray blobs, and the one with sealing comes out clean.]
## Nothing Purges
[画像: Nothing purges: the cost of color.]
Single-nozzle printers push the old color out before every change, and it goes straight in the bin. Quadro’s heads never share a nozzle, so there’s nothing to push out. Same four-color model: 1,079 g of waste on a single-nozzle printer, 135 g on Quadro. That’s 87.5% less. ²
[画像: Scale test: the same four-color model printed on Quadro with a small prime tower beside it, and on a single-nozzle printer with a box full of purge waste.]
[画像: Scale test counters: 87.5% less filament waste on Quadro, with a counter of the filament saved.]
[画像: Zero Waste Mode: no tower, no waste.]
Quadro never purges. When a head resumes printing, a small prime tower usually steadies nozzle pressure. On compatible models with enough infill, Zero Waste Mode skips the tower and does it inside the infill, where no one will ever see it. Not a gram wasted between colors. ⁵
[画像: Zero Waste Mode switched on: zero-waste printing on compatible models with no prime tower, because pressure equalization happens inside the infill.]
Zero Waste Mode No prime tower. No purge. Zero color-change waste. On compatible models.
[画像: Savings calculator: same filament, five times the prints.]
With the Co Print Quadro Simulator, you can test Quadro using your own 3D models before purchasing one. Simply upload a model sliced in any slicer. The simulator processes it using the same print settings across different slicers, including Co Print Slicer, OrcaSlicer, and Snapmaker Slicer, automatically comparing print times and filament waste.
It also accurately simulates Quadro's real printing process, letting you see its four independent toolheads in action and exactly how your model would be printed.
So, how big is the difference?
Take a 30 g four-color model and 4 kg of filament. A single-nozzle printer wasting 119 g per print gets just 26 finished models. With Quadro's Zero Waste Mode, you can produce up to 133 prints using the same amount of filament.
That's over five times more finished prints from the same filament!
Want to see your own savings? Choose your model, how often you print, and what you pay for filament. Discover how much time and material you could save with Quadro.
→ https://calculator.coprint3d.com/
[画像: Quadro Simulator demo: a four-color cube file is dropped in and simulated on Quadro, and the counters show 4 kg of filament making 133 cubes of 30 g on Quadro with 0 g waste, against 26 on a single-nozzle printer that wastes 119 g per print.]
## Make More
[画像: Make more: what will you print?]
Figures, cosplay, functional parts and gifts. Everything here came off a Quadro. Whether you’re a hobbyist, a designer, an engineer or running a print farm, Quadro fits right into your workflow.
[画像: One printer, endless possibilities: Quadro prints for cosplay, hobby, design, engineering, home and print farms.]
## Multi Material 3D Printing
[画像: Multi-material: four materials, one print.]
Load up to four materials and print them in one go. Rigid bodies with flexible grips, strong parts with soluble supports, all in a single continuous print, with no post-processing or assembly in between. Four heads at four temperatures, and far more you can design.
[画像: A part printed with soluble PVA supports dropped into water, where the supports dissolve and leave the surface clean.]
Print supports in soluble PVA, drop the part in water, and the surface underneath comes out untouched.
[画像: Quadro printing a functional part in two materials, then the finished part being lifted off the plate.]
Combine different materials in a single print to create durable, functional parts for industrial applications.
[画像: Flexible TPU 95A prints from Quadro: a red and black grip bending in the hand, and shoe soles printed in TPU and PLA.]
Quadro can easily print TPU 95A and similar flexible materials, even combining them with PLA in a single multi-material print.
## Room to Print Big
[画像: 300 × 300 × 300 mm: room to print big.]
Quadro features a spacious 300 × 300 × 300 mm build volume, 61% more than standard 256 mm machines.⁶ Print a full helmet, a cosplay piece or a batch of parts in one job, without splitting and gluing. Every toolhead reaches the entire bed, so all four colors are there wherever your model needs them.
[画像: 61% larger build volume than a standard 256 mm printer: the same football helmet in a 256 mm cube (16.8 L) and in Quadro's 300 mm cube (27.0 L).]
[画像: Quadro Enclosure: built for tougher parts.]
Engineering filaments warp and crack when the air around them can’t hold its heat. The Quadro Enclosure is an optional add-on that keeps the build environment steady, with built-in air filtration. Add it when your work calls for strong, heat-resistant parts.
[画像: Quadro inside the optional Quadro Enclosure, with a chamber temperature readout for warp-free engineering materials such as ABS and ASA.]
## More From Four Heads
[画像: Free updates: more from four heads.]
Four independent toolheads can do more than change colors. These features are in development and testing on Quadro now, and they'll come to every Quadro as free updates. Our goal is to have them live by the time Quadro reaches you.
[画像: CMYK Full Color: in testing.]
[画像: CMYK 3D printing, in testing on Quadro: a full-color lighthouse model blended layer by layer from cyan, magenta, yellow and black.]
Load cyan, magenta, yellow and black, and Co Slicer stacks thin layers of them to blend new shades, so four spools can print smooth gradients and full-color models. Results depend on the filament and the model, and we'll share our test prints as they come off the line.
[画像: Multi nozzle sizes: in testing.]
…(以下省略)
risks: Quadro is our third Kickstarter. We delivered our first two campaigns, MFM in 2021 and ChromaSet in 2023, to more than 1,500 backers, and we've shipped Co Print products to over 10,000 makers in 64 countries. Quadro has been in development for two years, has been shown publicly since December 2025, and is now running on a pilot production line with our manufacturing partner in China, with units already in reviewers' hands. Bringing a new printer to mass production still carries risk, and we'd rather tell you exactly what we're watching. Production scaling. Moving from pilot runs to mass production can bring variation in part consistency, assembly yield or supplier lead times. We're using the pilot line to find and fix issues before the main run, and we're ordering long-lead components as soon as the campaign ends. Every Quadro is calibrated and test-printed before it ships. Four-toolhead precision. Keeping four independent toolheads aligned print after print depends on tight coordination between mechanics, calibration and firmware. Quadro calibrates toolhead offsets automatically, and we're running long-duration reliability tests on the pilot units. If early production needs refinement, we'll fix it before it ships, not after. Software. QuadrOS and Co Slicer are in active development and testing with our community. Anything that isn't ready for the first shipments will be stated clearly on this page and delivered later as a free software update. Certification, shipping and customs. CE, FCC and UKCA certification is in progress. Shipping times and import rules can change, especially for the US. Shipping rates shown are estimates, and we'll confirm your final cost in the pledge manager before you pay. If something slips. Our delivery estimate includes buffer. If anything changes, you'll hear it from us first, in an update with the reason and the new date. Rewards ship in pledge order, reservation holders first, and we'll post a production update every month until the last Quadro is delivered. With our team in Istanbul, support in the UK and US, and production partners in China, we're set up to support Quadro well after it arrives.

faq.q: Product | What is Co Print Quadro?
faq.a: Quadro is a multicolor, multi-material 3D printer with four independent toolheads on a single X-axis, a design we call IQEX™. Each head has its own motor, filament path and nozzle, so colors never share a nozzle and nothing is swapped between colors.

faq.q: Product | How is Quadro different from toolchangers and AMS-style printers?
faq.a: Single-nozzle systems purge the old color on every change. Tool and nozzle changers pick heads or nozzles up and put them down. Quadro keeps all four heads mounted and loaded: one slides out of the way and the next takes its place in about a second, with no purge and no swap.

faq.q: Product | How long does a color change take?
faq.a: About one second of mechanical movement: T1→T2 1.00 s, T1→T3 1.40 s, T1→T4 1.57 s. The next head starts heating about 30 seconds early and waits sealed in its QDock Station. Priming can add time depending on the job.

faq.q: Product | Does Quadro still use a prime tower?
faq.a: Quadro never purges, because no two colors share a nozzle. A small prime tower can be used to steady nozzle pressure. On compatible models with enough infill, Zero Waste Mode does this inside the infill instead, so no tower is printed.

faq.q: Product | Can all four heads reach the full build volume?
faq.a: Yes. Every head reaches the whole 300 × 300 × 300 mm volume, so all four colors are available anywhere on the plate.

faq.q: Product | What features are coming after launch?
faq.a: CMYK full-color printing, mixed nozzle sizes in one print, and print-farm tools in the Co Print App (a shared job queue, a model library and AI-assisted print management) are in development and testing. They'll come to every Quadro as free updates; our goal is to have them live by the time Quadro reaches you. Multi-color dual printing, two prints at once in two colors each, already runs on Quadro.

faq.q: Product | Is Quadro a good fit for print farms?
faq.a: Yes. No color-clearing purge and a 300 × 300 mm plate suit batches of multicolor parts. The Farm Pack includes four Quadros, an Enclosure, a Filament Dryer 4-Pack, a Spare Parts Kit, Co Print Care on every unit, a free Watchtower Hobby license for up to 5 printers and 40% off Meshy Studio for 12 months.

faq.q: Product | I already own a Co Print kit. Is Quadro for me?
faq.a: Our upgrade kits add color to printers you already own. Quadro is a complete printer built around four independent toolheads, for anyone who wants a dedicated multicolor, multi-material machine.

faq.q: Product | Can I see Quadro in person?
faq.a: Yes, at Formnext 2026 in Frankfurt, November 17–20, Hall 12.1, Booth G89. After that, CES 2027 in USA.

faq.q: Materials | Which materials can Quadro print?
faq.a: PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA and PLA-CF on the open frame, and ABS and ASA with the optional Quadro Enclosure. Each head holds its own material at its own temperature, so you can combine up to four materials in one print.

faq.q: Materials | Can I use third-party filament?
faq.a: Yes. Quadro is an open material platform: use any 1.75 mm filament brand you like. Material presets are on the touchscreen.

faq.q: Materials | Do I need the enclosure?
faq.a: Not for PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA or PLA-CF, which print on the open frame. The optional Quadro Enclosure keeps the build environment steady for ABS and ASA, with built-in air filtration

faq.q: Software | Which software does Quadro use? Is it open source?
faq.a: Quadro runs QuadrOS, built on Klipper, and Co Slicer, built on OrcaSlicer for Windows, macOS and Linux. Co Slicer is already open source on GitHub, and the QuadrOS source will follow. The Co Print App for Android and iOS lets you start, watch and queue prints, and run several Quadros from one screen.

faq.q: Software | Can I try Quadro with my own models before backing?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a model to the Quadro Simulator at calculator.coprint3d.com to compare print time and filament waste, and watch Quadro's four toolheads print it.

faq.q: Campaign | When will I be charged?
faq.a: Only when the campaign ends, and only if Quadro reaches its funding goal. Kickstarter collects the payment.
